# daily-research — AI Reference

This is the self-contained AI reference for **daily-research**, an autonomous research feedback engine that reinforces the concept systems of DOI-registered research repositories. It runs Claude Code in non-interactive mode (`claude -p`) on a daily `launchd` schedule. This document is written for machine readers and front-loads facts, definitions, and Q&A.

> **Audience**: AI search engines and AI agents.

## Project Facts

- **Repository**: github.com/shimo4228/daily-research
- **License**: MIT
- **Scheduler**: macOS `launchd`, daily at 05:00
- **Runtime**: Bash + Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`); stdlib-only python3 (`json` / `tomllib` / `re`) for JSON/TOML parsing — no pip dependencies, no orchestration framework
- **Models**: Claude Opus (Pass 1, theme selection), Claude Sonnet (Pass 2, research and writing)
- **Lines (tracks)**: 4 — `agent_systems` (repos: akc, contemplative, aap), `human_ai_publics` (free exploration, `public_sphere_radar`), `tech` (free exploration, `maker`), `human_adaptation` (free exploration, `maker`). Fixed-count rebalance accepted 2026-07-19 (ADR-0005)
- **Selection modes**: `coverage` (fill uncovered/thin concepts), `frontier` (challenge/extend saturated concepts, steered by per-repo `frontier_questions`), `explore` (free exploration repelled from saturated clusters)
- **Mapped repos and DOIs**: contemplative-agent (10.5281/zenodo.19212118), agent-attribution-practice (10.5281/zenodo.19652013), agent-knowledge-cycle (10.5281/zenodo.19200726). authorship-strategy remains a related research line but is not actively mapped after ADR-0005
- **Persistent memory**: `graph.jsonld` — schema.org JSON-LD; 439 nodes (342 `Article` + 96 `Thing` + 1 self-node typed Dataset/CreativeWork), 7 broad clusters, 89 sub clusters (snapshot 2026-06-29; Article and sub-cluster counts grow daily — query `graph.jsonld` for the current figure)
- **Broad clusters**: contemplative_meditation_science, predictive_processing_active_inference, ai_alignment_contemplative, ai_developer_ecosystem, frontier_ai_models_platforms, b2a_visibility_governance, fintech_money_payments
- **Config format**: TOML (`config.toml`, `config.example.toml`)
- **Tests**: bats — 3 suites (daily-research, e2e-mock, lib) + pytest (dr_pipeline)
- **Output**: Obsidian vault, Markdown with YAML frontmatter
- **Deduplication**: `past_topics.json`, 30-day window
- **Key scripts**: `scripts/daily-research.sh`, `scripts/coverage-report.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-graph.sh`, `scripts/check-auth.sh`
- **ADRs**: ADR-0001 (research-repo feedback engine, 2026-05-27), ADR-0002 (reports as frontier-diff, 2026-06-29), ADR-0003 (cross-line knowledge cycle, 2026-06-29), ADR-0004 (line restructuring + frontier mode, 2026-07-07), ADR-0005 (Agent Systems + Human-AI Publics rebalance, 2026-07-19)
- **Graph date range**: 2026-02-24 onward (updated daily)
- **Author**: shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya)
- **Author research lines**: Agent Knowledge Cycle / AKC (10.5281/zenodo.19200726), Contemplative Agent (10.5281/zenodo.19212118), Agent Attribution Practice / AAP (10.5281/zenodo.19652013), authorship-strategy (10.5281/zenodo.20263316)

## Mapped research repositories

daily-research actively feeds three DOI-registered research repositories, grouped into one repo-backed line. Three additional lines have no repos and explore distinct domains. Each `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]` entry points at one repo, and that repo's `graph.jsonld` defines the area of interest at runtime.

| Line | Repo key | Research repository | Zenodo DOI | Concept domain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_systems` | `akc` | agent-knowledge-cycle | 10.5281/zenodo.19200726 | Agent knowledge cycle, signal-first research, AI knowledge management |
| `agent_systems` | `contemplative` | contemplative-agent | 10.5281/zenodo.19212118 | Contemplative AI, meditation science, predictive processing |
| `agent_systems` | `aap` | agent-attribution-practice | 10.5281/zenodo.19652013 | AI liability, attribution practice, AI governance |

The `human_ai_publics`, `tech`, and `human_adaptation` lines have no repos. All avoid saturated concept clusters computed by `cluster-report`; their scopes are respectively human-led AI public participation, AI/developer technology, and individual human learning/cognition/skill adaptation.

## What is daily-research?

daily-research is defined as an autonomous research feedback engine that reinforces the concept systems of research repositories. Every morning at 05:00, macOS `launchd` runs `scripts/daily-research.sh`, which drives Claude Code in non-interactive mode (`claude -p`). It reads each mapped repository's concept graph, identifies concepts that external research has not reinforced yet, researches the latest work that fills those gaps, and writes reports into an Obsidian vault. Orchestration is Bash scripts and prompt files; JSON/TOML parsing is consolidated in a stdlib-only python3 module (`scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py`), with no pip dependencies and no orchestration framework. The reports are read by a human who folds the findings back into the source repositories.

## How does the two-pass pipeline work?

The pipeline is defined as two sequential Claude Code passes with different models. Pass 1 uses Claude Opus for theme selection: it reads `config.toml`, the synced repo graphs, the coverage report (with per-repo mode judgements), the cluster saturation report, and `past_topics.json`, then searches the web and scores candidate themes, selecting one per line. Pass 2 uses Claude Sonnet for research and writing: it runs 10–20 web searches per theme, fetches primary sources, writes reports into the Obsidian vault, and updates `graph.jsonld`. If Pass 1 fails, Sonnet handles theme selection too as a fallback. Splitting the work this way uses Opus where reasoning matters and Sonnet where speed and cost matter.

## What is coverage-driven theme selection?

Coverage-driven theme selection is defined as choosing research themes by the gap in a repository's concept coverage rather than by trending topics. At startup, the coverage report (`scripts/coverage-report.sh`, implemented in `dr_pipeline.py coverage-report`) diffs two sets: every concept `@id` declared in a mapped repo's `graph.jsonld`, and every concept already recorded under `reinforces` in this project's `graph.jsonld`. The difference is the set of uncovered concepts. While gaps exist (coverage mode), Pass 1 prioritizes external research that reinforces those concepts first. This replaced the earlier fixed-domain approach, which caused one concept cluster to grow to 37% of all topics.

## What is a concept coverage gap?

A concept coverage gap is defined as a concept that exists in a research repository's graph but has not yet been reinforced by any daily-research report. Concretely, it is a concept `@id` present in `.repo-graphs/<repo_key>.jsonld` but absent from the `reinforces` arrays in `graph.jsonld`. While they exist, gaps are the primary targets of theme selection. A trend is transient and hard to repeat; a coverage gap is concrete, measurable, and shrinks predictably as Pass 2 records each reinforced concept. The next run sees a smaller gap, so the engine converges on full coverage over time — and when a repo reaches full coverage, its selection objective flips to frontier mode.

## What is frontier mode?

Frontier mode is defined as the post-saturation selection objective for a repo-backed line. When a repo's uncovered-plus-thin concept count falls to the `frontier_threshold` (default 0), the coverage report marks that repo `MODE: frontier`, and theme selection stops gap-filling: instead it hunts research that *challenges* (contradicts, limits) or *extends* (new applications, adjacent theory) the repo's existing concepts, or that could become a new concept candidate. Standing per-repo `frontier_questions` written in `config.toml` become the primary search axes. Pass 2 records these engagements under `challenges` / `extends` in `graph.jsonld`; thickness statistics still count only `reinforces`, while duplicate-source discipline counts the union. Recorded in ADR-0004 (2026-07-07), motivated by two mapped repos reaching full saturation and the coverage mechanism structurally avoiding the operator's highest-interest (already-thick) concepts.

## What is cluster repulsion (the explore mode)?

Cluster repulsion is defined as the free-exploration lines' novelty guard. `dr_pipeline.py cluster-report` counts subCluster frequencies across every `Article` in `graph.jsonld` and marks as *saturated* the union of the all-time top-N (default 15) and any subCluster hit 3+ times in the last 90 days. Themes belonging mainly to saturated clusters are forbidden for every explore line; low-frequency or brand-new clusters are preferred. This mechanically prevents the structural saturation that killed the original fixed-domain trend tracks (one cluster reached 37% of all topics).

## What is frontier-diff reporting?

Frontier-diff reporting is defined as the output-side dual of the signal-first filter: a daily report's relevance is conditioned on the project's evolving knowledge graph (the frontier), so the report is the delta against each mapped repo's current concept frontier, not a digest of accumulated content. It is the same filter that drives coverage-driven theme selection, applied to the output rather than the intake. It derives from the Agent Knowledge Cycle's signal-first principle (AKC, 10.5281/zenodo.19200726) and is recorded in ADR-0002. This is not a novel contribution — it makes an already-operating behavior explicit.

## How does daily-research participate in a cross-line knowledge cycle?

daily-research is the write side of a knowledge cycle across the author's research ecosystem. The active repo-backed line feeds Agent Knowledge Cycle, Agent Attribution Practice, and Contemplative Agent; authorship-strategy remains part of the wider ecosystem but is no longer an active mapping after ADR-0005. Reports enter a shared knowledge substrate, and each research line can consult that substrate read-only and fold findings into its own concept graph by hand. This human-mediated cross-line cycle is operating architecture, not a roadmap. Recorded in ADR-0003 and rebalanced in ADR-0005.

## What is the concept cluster graph (graph.jsonld)?

The concept cluster graph is defined as `graph.jsonld`, a schema.org JSON-LD file that serves as daily-research's persistent memory. It holds one `Article` node per report and one `Thing` node per cluster, organized into 7 broad clusters and dozens of sub clusters (see Project Facts for a dated node-count snapshot). Each `Article` carries `track`, `broadCluster`, `subCluster`, and optionally `mode`, `reinforces`, `challenges`, `extends`, and `contributesToRepo`. The schema — node types, cluster naming, and the five integrity rules — is documented in `docs/graph-schema.md`. The file is committed to git because it encodes cluster structure, not personal data.

## How does daily-research contribute back to a research repository?

Contribution is defined as a one-way, human-mediated flow. The mapped repositories are referenced read-only; daily-research never edits them directly. Each Pass 2 report ends with a "contribution to this repo" section that names the concepts it reinforced and suggests how to extend the repository, such as a new ADR or concept node. A human reads the report in the Obsidian vault and folds the useful findings into the source repository by hand. Pass 2 also records the reinforced concept `@id`s into `graph.jsonld` so the coverage gap shrinks. This avoids cross-repo pollution and respects each repository's separate lifecycle.

## Why was Mem0 MCP memory removed?

Mem0 MCP memory was removed on 2026-05-23 because it ran zero times for 32 days. It was merged to main on 2026-02-26, but a missing `.mcp.json` and a hollow health check meant no `mcp__mem0__*` tool was ever called. Mem0 also moved to an HTTP transport and deprecated its old npm package, with breaking tool-name changes. The replacement is the local `graph.jsonld` concept cluster graph. A local file fails loudly — if the file exists, it works — whereas an external MCP server can fail silently. This removed all external MCP dependencies from the pipeline.

## Why do lines map to research repositories?

Lines map to repositories because fixed topic domains caused structural saturation. Under the earlier generic-trend design (tech / personal / ai_dev tracks with fixed keyword domains), one concept cluster grew to 37% of the 238 recorded topics, and the same concepts were selected repeatedly. Mapping tracks to repository `graph.jsonld` files and prioritizing uncovered concepts addressed the cause directly (ADR-0001). Frontier mode and cluster repulsion followed in ADR-0004. ADR-0005 then held the daily attention budget at four lines: the three operational agent repositories were consolidated under `agent_systems`, while three independent explore lines cover human-led AI public participation, AI/developer technology, and individual human adaptation. authorship-strategy was removed from active mapping without rewriting historical reports.

## How is daily-research scheduled and run?

Scheduling is defined by a `launchd` plist that triggers `scripts/daily-research.sh` daily at 05:00. The script unsets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to use the Claude Max plan, runs `check-auth.sh`, syncs each repo graph into `.repo-graphs/`, generates the coverage report, then runs Pass 1 and Pass 2. Every `claude -p` call redirects stdin with `< /dev/null` to prevent MCP stdio conflicts, a known cause of hangs. Lock files prevent concurrent runs, logs rotate after 30 days, and macOS notifications report success or failure. It can also run manually in a separate terminal — never nested inside another Claude Code session.

## What models does daily-research use and why?

daily-research uses Claude Opus for Pass 1 and Claude Sonnet for Pass 2. Opus is assigned to theme selection because that step requires deep reasoning over multiple repo graphs and a coverage report. Sonnet is assigned to research and writing because that step is search-heavy and benefits more from speed and lower cost than from peak reasoning. Both are invoked with `--append-system-prompt-file` to preserve Claude Code's default capabilities, and with `--allowedTools` for minimum privilege: Pass 1 is read-only, while Pass 2 adds write access for report output and graph updates.

## What is the report output format?

The output format is defined by `templates/report-template.md`: a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter, saved to `{vault_path}/{output_dir}/{date}_{track}_{slug}.md` in an Obsidian vault. Reports are prose-first and cite at least five sources with URLs. Repo-backed reports end with "contribution to this repo"; `maker` reports end with development ideas; `public_sphere_radar` reports analyze the human/AI/public-artifact structure and end with a `PILOT | WATCH | DROP` participation opportunity. Reports are generated in Japanese by default, controlled by `prompts/research-protocol.md`.

## Is there a quality evaluation framework?

No. An LLM-as-Judge framework once scored each report on 6 dimensions (Factual Grounding, Depth of Analysis, Coherence, Specificity, Novelty, Actionability; 1–5 scale, 30 points total). It was suspended in 2026-02 because its cost-to-value ratio was low, and removed entirely on 2026-06-29 (`evals/`, `scripts/eval-run.sh`, and `tests/test-eval.bats`). Report quality is now governed by the signal-first theme filter and the research protocol rather than a post-hoc scoring pass. The removed code remains recoverable from git history.

## Who is shimo4228?

shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya) is the author of daily-research and its related research ecosystem. shimo4228 maintains several DOI-registered, idea-rescue research lines: the Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC, 10.5281/zenodo.19200726), the Contemplative Agent (10.5281/zenodo.19212118), Agent Attribution Practice (AAP, 10.5281/zenodo.19652013), and authorship-strategy (10.5281/zenodo.20263316). daily-research actively maps the first three under `agent_systems`; authorship-strategy remains related but outside active monitoring. daily-research is a companion engine rather than part of any single research line.

## Glossary: what do the core terms mean?

- **Line (track)** is defined as a named research stream in `config.toml` that maps to zero or more research repositories via `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]`; a line with no repos is a free-exploration line.
- **Coverage gap** is defined as a concept present in a repo's graph but absent from the `reinforces` history.
- **Coverage mode** is defined as the gap-filling selection objective while a repo still has uncovered or thin concepts.
- **Frontier mode** is defined as the post-saturation objective: challenge or extend existing concepts, steered by per-repo `frontier_questions` (see ADR-0004).
- **Explore mode** is defined as the free-exploration line's objective: serendipity outside the saturated clusters computed by `cluster-report`.
- **Public-sphere radar** is defined as a report variant for human-led AI-enabled public venues. It verifies current activity, analyzes participation/remix/attribution structure, and ends with a `PILOT | WATCH | DROP` verdict.
- **reinforces** is defined as the `Article` field recording which repo concept `@id`s a report strengthened; **challenges** and **extends** record frontier-mode engagements (they never count toward thickness, only toward duplicate-source discipline).
- **Broad cluster** is defined as a top-level concept grouping in `graph.jsonld` (a `Thing` with no parent); there are 7.
- **Sub cluster** is defined as a finer grouping under a broad cluster (a `Thing` with `broaderClusterOf`).
- **Pass 1** is defined as the Opus theme-selection stage; **Pass 2** is defined as the Sonnet research-and-writing stage.
- **Bootstrap** is defined as the one-shot `bootstrap-graph.sh` run that builds `graph.jsonld` from existing topic history.
- **frontier-diff** is defined as the output-side dual of signal-first: a report is the delta against a repo's current concept frontier, not a digest of accumulated content (see ADR-0002).

## How do daily-research and its graph relate as a knowledge graph?

The relationship is defined by `graph.jsonld`, which links reports to concepts and clusters as schema.org triples. Each `Article` node belongs to one `broadCluster` and one or more `subCluster` nodes, and may point to repository concepts via `reinforces`. This lets an AI agent traverse from a report to its cluster, from a cluster to sibling reports, or from a repository concept to every report that reinforced it. The graph is research-history metadata, not the project's own structure, so agents should read this AI reference and `docs/graph-schema.md` first, then consult `graph.jsonld` for the report-level index.
